titles.231: Annotatio III §.VII open: POSTERIUS — CASSELLANUM (this century’s second Protestant-peace molimen) claims three peculiarities
titles.232: Annotatio III §.VII (1): Careful weighing of disputed dogmas; consensus and dissent marked without varnish; modest judgment on weight more than bare truth — consciences unhurt
titles.233: Annotatio III §.VII (2a): After full examination — Evangelicals agree on the Foundation of Faith and Salvation; disputed questions do not overturn that foundation
titles.234: Annotatio III §.VII (2b): Remaining controversies — not for pulpits, or only with utmost modesty; schools and academies likewise without persecution or personal naming (Autor p. 330)
titles.235: Annotatio III §.VII (3) close: Defense of the charitable colloquy; Rinteln Epistola Apologetica; Maresius/Hornbeck/Heidegger — stop before §.VIII

latin.231:
§. VII.
POSTERIUS hujus Seculi Molimen Pacis Protestanticae, CASSELLANUM puta, tria alia sibi peculiaria vindicat:
latin.232: (1.) Quòd specialium Dogmatum controversorum momenta accuratè expenderit, Consensum Dissensumque ubique, citra fucum, annotaverit, & tum demum de Consensûs Dissensûsque Pondere magis, quàm Veritate, modestum judicium, illaesis utrinque Conscienciis, tulerit.
latin.233: (2.) Quòd omnibus ritè examinatis, ingenuè cordatéque statuerit, convenire Evangelicis de Fundamento Fidei & Salutis: Quaestiones Controversas fundamentum istud minus attingere, minus multò tollere aut evertere;
latin.234: & ne pars altera deinceps propter dissensum aliqualem, alteram, vel convitiis proscinderet, vel damnaret, consultum putaverit conveneritque, Controversias, quae adhuc superessent, aut non tractandas fore in Ecclesiis pro Concione, aut certè summâ cum modestia, si Necessitas planè exigeret, Dissentientium nulla mentione, nulla Verborum asperitate, nullis Consequentis affictis, sola veritatis ex Scriptura declaratione; In Scholis verò & Academiis magna pariter cum moderatione citra insectationem, citra Personalia, aut nominum indicia, quicquid reliqvum esset controversorum Capitum, tractaretur. Autor p. 330.
latin.235: (3.) Quòd utraque Colloquentium pars colloquium suum Charitativum contra obtrectatores Pacisque Protestanticae osores quoscunque, impigre doctéque defenderit, & exterorum Protestantium propemodum omnium amplissimum applausum meruerit; Rintelensium etiam Epistola Apologetica, sublimis Judicii ac multijugae Eruditionis Theologorum biga, Petro Museo & Joh. Hennichio Auctoribus debita, in alias linguas translata sit. Confer Defension. Colloq. Cassel. Maresii, Hornbeckii, Heideggeri &c.

pass_a.231: §. VII. The LATER Effort of Protestant Peace in this century, namely the CASSEL one, claims for itself three other peculiarities:
pass_a.232: (1.) That it carefully weighed the moments of the special disputed Dogmas, annotated Consensus and Dissensus everywhere without varnish, and only then rendered a modest judgment concerning the Weight of Consensus and Dissensus more than concerning Truth, with consciences on both sides unhurt.
pass_a.233: (2.) That when all things had been duly examined, it candidly and heartily determined that Evangelicals agree concerning the Foundation of Faith and Salvation: that the Controverted Questions less touch that foundation, and much less take it away or overturn it;
pass_a.234: and lest one party thereafter, because of some dissent, should either tear the other with insults or condemn it, it judged advisable and agreed that Controversies still remaining were either not to be treated in the Churches from the pulpit, or certainly with the utmost modesty if Necessity plainly required it — with no mention of Dissenters, no harshness of words, no forged Consequences, only a declaration of truth from Scripture; but in Schools and Academies likewise with great moderation, without persecution, without Personals or name-pointing, whatever remained of the controverted Heads should be treated. Author p. 330.
pass_a.235: (3.) That either party of the Colloquents diligently and learnedly defended their Charitable colloquy against detractors and whatever haters of Protestant Peace, and earned the fullest applause of almost all foreign Protestants; that even the Rinteln Apologetic Letter — owed to a pair of Theologians of sublime Judgment and manifold Erudition, Peter Musaeus and John Hennichius as Authors — was translated into other languages. Compare the Defense of the Cassel Colloquy of Maresius, Hornbeck, Heidegger, etc.

231: §. VII. This century’s later Protestant-peace Consociation attempt — the Cassel one — claims three peculiarities of its own:
232: (1.) It carefully weighed the force of the special disputed doctrines, marked consensus and dissent everywhere without varnish,
and only then gave a modest judgment on the weight of that consensus and dissent more than on bare truth — leaving both sides’ consciences unhurt.
233: (2.) After everything was duly examined, it candidly and heartily judged that Evangelicals agree on the Foundation of Faith and Salvation:
the disputed questions touch that foundation less — and still less tear it up or overturn it;
234: and lest either side next tear or damn the other for some leftover dissent, they judged it wise and agreed:

remaining controversies should not be handled from church pulpits — or if necessity plainly forced it, only with utmost modesty, naming no dissenters, using no harsh words, forging no consequences, declaring truth from Scripture alone;
and in schools and academies likewise with great moderation, without persecution, personal attacks, or name-pointing (Autor p. 330).
235: (3.) Both colloquy sides vigorously and learnedly defended their charitable colloquy against detractors and every hater of Protestant peace, and won near-universal applause from foreign Protestants.
Even the Rinteln Epistola Apologetica — by that pair of high-judgment, many-sided theologians Peter Musaeus and John Hennichius — was translated into other languages.
Compare the Cassel Colloquy defenses of Maresius, Hornbeck, Heidegger, and others.
Stop before §. VIII (fruits of Lipsiacum and Cassellanum into the present age).
